cands.bio: Democrat who has served in the Alabama Senate (District 19) since 2022. She was in the Alabama House (District 57) from 2002 to 2022 and became House Assistant Minority Leader in 2017. She founded the Law Offices of Merika Coleman and worked as a policy analyst. She ran for Congress in 2024.
cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Coleman on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police pay, or school choice and teacher pay. We couldn't confirm where she was raised or when she came to Alabama, and her birthplace comes from a single source. No endorsements were identified for her 2026 race. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, and her campaign site has no issue positions. Claims on her campaign site about courtroom and bench experience were not verified elsewhere.

qual.background: Alabama House member 2002-2022 and Assistant Minority Leader from 2017, then state senator from 2022. Earlier she was a public policy analyst, an economic development director at Lawson State Community College and for the City of Bessemer, and founder of a law office (J.D. 2017, M.P.A. 1997).
qual.why: More than 20 years of legislative service, including a chamber leadership post, plus policy, public administration and law careers, fit the high band for writing law and the budget.
